headings.title: Valuation of pecuniary distribution to spouse
headings.reviewNote: Requires property distributed in satisfaction of a pecuniary bequest or transfer to a spouse to fairly reflect proportionate appreciation or depreciation when not valued at distribution-date fair market value.

headings.title: Valuation when instrument silent on in-kind distribution
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that property distributed in kind to satisfy a pecuniary bequest or transfer is valued at fair market value on the date of distribution when the instrument is silent.

headings.title: Definition of pecuniary bequest or transfer
headings.reviewNote: Defines pecuniary bequest or transfer as a bequest or transfer in a stated amount or in an amount determined by formula.

headings.title: Effective date and applicability to wills and trusts
headings.reviewNote: Establishes effective date of October 13, 1969, for wills, revocable inter vivos trusts where decedent dies on or after that date, and post-1969 irrevocable inter vivos trusts.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 456.001 governing in-kind valuation for spousal bequests, valuation rules when instrument is silent, statutory definition, and 1969 effective date.

headings.title: Methods of creating health savings account trust
headings.reviewNote: Permits creating a health savings account trust or custodial account under 26 U.S.C. Section 223(d)(1) (source footnote notes '223(c)(1)' appears in original rolls as an incorrect reference) by transfer of moneys, record documentation, or agreement execution.

headings.title: Deemed establishment date for beneficiary eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Deems an HSA trust or custodial account established on the first day in that calendar year the beneficiary is an eligible individual under 26 U.S.C. Section 223(c)(1).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.006 covering creation methods and deemed establishment date for health savings account trusts or custodial accounts, noting original-rolls reference error in note.

headings.title: Personal property lease deposits as trust funds
headings.reviewNote: Provides that lessee deposits or advance payments on personal property leases are trust funds deposited in a bank within seven days without commingling, imposes a misdemeanor penalty for violations, and exempts leases where property is delivered at agreement and remains in lessee's continuous possession.

headings.title: Exceptions for financial institutions and commercial leases
headings.reviewNote: Exempts leases entered into by banks, trust companies, savings and loan associations, savings banks, credit unions (and affiliates), section 381.410(4) financial institutions, or other lessors in commercial lease transactions of at least $25,000.

entries.reviewSummary: Personal property lease deposits held as non-commingled trust funds within seven days, misdemeanor penalty, possession exception, and financial-institution and $25,000 commercial lease exemptions.

headings.title: Prohibited actions for private foundations and charitable trusts
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits trustees of private foundations, charitable trusts, or split-interest trusts from engaging in acts of self-dealing, retaining excess business holdings, making jeopardizing investments, or making taxable expenditures under IRC sections 4941, 4943, 4944, and 4945.

headings.title: Required distributions to avoid excise tax liability
headings.reviewNote: Requires trustees to distribute amounts at least sufficient to avoid liability for tax imposed by IRC Section 4942(a).

headings.title: Court determination of contrary governing terms and immunity
headings.reviewNote: Provides subsections 1 and 2 do not apply if a court determines application is contrary to the trust instrument and insulates trustee from liability for prior payments.

headings.title: Preservation of court and attorney general authority
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that the section does not impair the rights and powers of Missouri courts or the attorney general regarding trusts.

headings.title: Internal Revenue Code reference date
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that all references to the United States Internal Revenue Code refer to the law as of June 14, 1971.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 456.019 governing private foundation and charitable trust prohibited transactions, tax distribution requirements, court determinations, attorney general powers, and IRC reference date.

headings.title: Perpetuities exemption when trustee has power to sell
headings.reviewNote: Exempts trusts from the rule against perpetuities and restraint on alienation rules if the trustee or delegated person has the power to sell trust property.

headings.title: Rule against accumulations and discretionary distribution power
headings.reviewNote: Provides that rule against accumulations does not apply unless terms require accumulation beyond the perpetuities period, and grants discretionary distribution power during that period.

headings.title: Applicability to wills, agreements, and powers of appointment
headings.reviewNote: Defines prospective application to trusts created or amended on or after August 28, 2001, and out-of-state trusts moving to Missouri where perpetuities was inapplicable.

headings.title: Definition of trust and excluded arrangements
headings.reviewNote: Defines trust as express trust created by instrument or will with general administration, and lists excluded entities such as business, voting, and liquidation trusts.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 456.025 governing the Missouri rule against perpetuities exemption for trusts with power to sell, accumulation rules, effective dates, and trust definitions.

headings.title: Registration of trust in probate division
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes trustee of a trust having its principal place of administration in Missouri to register the trust in the probate division of the circuit court.

headings.title: Definition of trust for registration purposes
headings.reviewNote: Defines trust for registration purposes to include express private or charitable trusts and constructive trusts administered as express trusts, while excluding estate administrations, bank trust accounts, and business trusts.

headings.title: Determination of principal place of administration
headings.reviewNote: Specifies rules for determining the principal place of administration based on trust instrument designation, trustee place of business or residence, and cotrustee arrangements.

headings.title: Definition of professional fiduciary
headings.reviewNote: Defines professional fiduciary as an individual trustee who represents to the public having specialized training, experience, or skills in trust administration.

headings.title: Exception for retained foreign court jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Provides that registration does not apply if registration would be inconsistent with the retained jurisdiction of a foreign court.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 456.027 establishing procedures for trust registration in probate divisions, definitions of trust and professional fiduciary, and principal place of administration criteria.

headings.title: Trustee personal jurisdiction upon registration
headings.reviewNote: Provides that registering a trust or accepting trusteeship of a registered trust submits the trustee personally to the court's jurisdiction for internal affairs proceedings, and specifies notice procedures.

headings.title: Beneficiary submission to court jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Subjects beneficiaries of a registered trust to court jurisdiction to the extent of their interests in internal affairs proceedings with notice under section 472.100.

headings.title: Definition of interested persons
headings.reviewNote: Defines interested persons to include beneficiaries, claimants with property rights against the trust estate, and fiduciaries representing them.

headings.title: Scope of internal affairs proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Defines internal affairs proceedings and enumerates 11 specific subject areas including trustee appointment, bond, accountings, investments, deviations, and trust termination.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 456.033 detailing jurisdictional effects of trust registration on trustees and beneficiaries, definitions of interested persons, and scope of internal affairs proceedings.

headings.title: Death certificate as prima facie proof
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that a certified or authenticated copy of a death certificate is prima facie proof of the fact, place, date, and time of death and identity of the decedent.

headings.title: Government records regarding person status as evidence
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a certified or authenticated copy of any governmental record that a person is missing, detained, dead, or alive is prima facie evidence of status and disclosed facts.

headings.title: Presumption of death after continuous five-year absence
headings.reviewNote: Creates a presumption of death for an individual absent for a continuous five-year period without explanation after diligent inquiry, effective at the end of the period unless evidence indicates earlier death.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.035 providing rules of evidence for establishing death or status through death certificates, governmental records, and the continuous 5-year absence presumption.

headings.title: Unclaimed property with unidentifiable beneficiaries
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes treating trust property as unclaimed when the trustee is unable to find or ascertain any heirs, representatives, or successors of a beneficiary after reasonable and diligent search.

headings.title: Unclaimed property after identified beneficiary failure to claim
headings.reviewNote: Permits deeming trust property unclaimed when an identified beneficiary fails or refuses to claim it for three years after a good-faith written notification attempt.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.037 specifying when trust property is deemed unclaimed due to unidentifiable beneficiaries or a 3-year failure to claim after written notice.

headings.title: Filing verified statement and transferring property to treasurer
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a trustee holding unclaimed trust property to file a verified statement detailing search efforts and instruments with the state treasurer and transfer the property in exchange for a receipt.

headings.title: Credit of transferred property to escheat fund
headings.reviewNote: Requires all unclaimed trust property received by the state treasurer under this section to be credited to the Missouri escheat fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.039 outlining procedures for filing verified statements with the state treasurer, property transfer, and crediting funds to the escheat fund.

headings.title: Discharge of trustee liability upon transfer to treasurer
headings.reviewNote: Provides that delivery of unclaimed property to the state treasurer terminates the relationship and releases the trustee from all liability to the beneficiary or heirs.

headings.title: Transfer pleadable as defense and bar to recovery
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes pleading the transfer of unclaimed property as a bar to recovery and complete defense against claims by apparent owners or successors.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.041 establishing complete discharge of trustee liability and affirmative defense upon transferring unclaimed property to the state treasurer.

headings.title: Standard of knowledge for individual
headings.reviewNote: Defines when a person has knowledge of a fact through actual knowledge, receipt of notice, or reason to know from all facts and circumstances.

headings.title: Knowledge and notice standard for organizations
headings.reviewNote: Specifies when an organization has notice or knowledge through responsible employees and defines organizational reasonable diligence.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.1-104 defining individual knowledge standards and organizational notice routines under the Missouri Uniform Trust Code.

headings.title: Default application of trust code provisions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that the Missouri Uniform Trust Code supplies default rules governing trustee duties, relations, and beneficiary rights except as provided in trust terms.

headings.title: Mandatory rules prevailing over trust terms
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates mandatory provisions that prevail over contrary trust terms, including creation requirements, good faith, beneficiary benefit, court powers, spendthrift protections, and notice duties.

headings.title: Permissible restrictions on trustee reporting duties
headings.reviewNote: Provides conditions and permissible limitations regarding the settlor's ability to restrict reporting duties to permissible distributees under subdivision (8) of subsection 2.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.1-105 setting default rules of the Missouri Uniform Trust Code and detailing mandatory statutory exceptions that cannot be overridden by trust terms.

headings.title: Validity of designated principal place of administration
headings.reviewNote: Validates trust term designating principal place of administration if trustee's business/residence or trust administration occurs in designated jurisdiction.

headings.title: Trustee authority to transfer principal place of administration
headings.reviewNote: Permits the trustee, without precluding court authority, to transfer the trust's principal place of administration to another state or foreign jurisdiction appropriate to the trust's purposes, administration, and beneficiaries' interests.

headings.title: Sixty-day notice of proposed transfer and contents
headings.reviewNote: Requires the trustee to notify qualified beneficiaries at least sixty days before initiating a transfer, specifying six mandatory notice items including new jurisdiction, contact info, reasons, governing-law warning, anticipated date, and objection deadline.

headings.title: Termination of nonjudicial transfer authority upon objection
headings.reviewNote: Terminates the trustee's authority to transfer the principal place of administration without a court order if a qualified beneficiary notifies the trustee of an objection on or before the specified date.

headings.title: Transfer of trust property to successor trustee
headings.reviewNote: Permits the trustee, in connection with transferring the principal place of administration, to transfer some or all trust property to a successor trustee designated in the trust or appointed under section 456.7-704.

entries.reviewSummary: Validity of designated principal place of administration, discretionary transfer authority, 60-day notice and required contents, termination of nonjudicial transfer upon objection, and transfer to successor trustee.

headings.title: Permissible methods of giving notice
headings.reviewNote: Provides that notice or document delivery must be accomplished by methods reasonably suitable under the circumstances, including first-class mail, personal delivery, or electronic messaging.

headings.title: Notice excused for unknown persons
headings.reviewNote: Excuses notice or document delivery if a person's identity or location is unknown and not reasonably ascertainable.

headings.title: Waiver of notice by recipient
headings.reviewNote: Permits the person to be notified or sent a document under sections 456.1-101 to 456.11-1106 to waive notice or document delivery.

headings.title: Notice requirements in judicial proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that notice of a judicial proceeding must be given in accordance with the applicable rules of civil procedure.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 456.1-109 outlining methods of notice, excused notice for unknown persons, waiver of notice, and civil procedure rules for judicial notice.

headings.title: Qualified beneficiary rights for charities and enforcers
headings.reviewNote: Grants qualified beneficiary rights under the UTC to a specified charitable organization or a person appointed to enforce an animal or noncharitable purpose trust under sections 456.4-408 or 456.4-409.

headings.title: Attorney general rights in charitable trusts
headings.reviewNote: Grants the Missouri attorney general qualified beneficiary rights (except under sections 456.1-108 and 456.4-411B) for a Missouri-administered charitable trust interest when no specified charitable organization is entitled to distribution and distributions would otherwise qualify one.

headings.title: Definition of specified charitable organization
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'specified charitable organization' as an identifiable charitable entity whose interest is not subject to a power of appointment or termination and that is or would be a permissible distributee on the determination date.

headings.title: Preservation of attorney general supervisory authority
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that no provision of this section limits the Missouri attorney general's authority to supervise and control charitable organizations.

entries.reviewSummary: Qualified beneficiary rights for specified charitable organizations, animal or noncharitable purpose trust enforcers, and the attorney general, plus definition of specified charitable organization and preserved attorney general authority.

headings.title: Definition of interested persons for nonjudicial settlements
headings.reviewNote: Defines interested persons for nonjudicial settlement agreements as persons whose consent would be required to achieve a binding settlement were the matter approved by the court.

headings.title: Authority to enter nonjudicial settlement agreement
headings.reviewNote: Permits interested persons, except as provided in subsections 3 and 6, to enter into a binding nonjudicial settlement agreement regarding any matter involving a trust.

headings.title: Validity limits and material purpose requirement
headings.reviewNote: Limits validity of a nonjudicial settlement agreement to the extent it does not violate a material purpose of the trust and includes terms properly approvable by the court.

headings.title: Matters resolvable by nonjudicial settlement
headings.reviewNote: Lists six non-exclusive matters resolvable by nonjudicial settlement agreement, including trust interpretation, report approval, trustee powers, resignation/appointment/compensation, administration transfer, and trustee liability.

headings.title: Court approval and adequacy of representation
headings.reviewNote: Permits any interested person to request court approval of a nonjudicial settlement agreement, determination of adequacy of representation under sections 456.3-301 to 456.3-305, and determination of proper terms.

headings.title: Prohibition on section 456.4-411B termination or modification
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits using a nonjudicial settlement agreement to terminate or modify a trust for reasons a court could do so under subsection 1 of section 456.4-411B.

entries.reviewSummary: Definition of interested persons, authorization and validity limits for nonjudicial settlement agreements, resolvable matters, court approval requests, and bar on section 456.4-411B(1) modifications or terminations.

headings.title: Revocation of spousal interests upon divorce
headings.reviewNote: Revokes beneficial terms and fiduciary appointments in a trust in favor of a former spouse or former spouse's relative upon marriage dissolution or annulment, giving effect as if they died immediately before finality.

headings.title: Exceptions where trust terms address divorce
headings.reviewNote: Exempts beneficial interests or fiduciary appointments created after dissolution or annulment or where trust terms expressly state dissolution or annulment shall not affect the designation.

headings.title: Agreements and orders preserving beneficial appointments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes settlors and spouses by binding agreement or court order to exempt a beneficial interest or fiduciary appointment from revocation.

headings.title: Revival of revoked provisions upon remarriage
headings.reviewNote: Revives trust terms revoked solely by this section upon remarriage of the settlor to the former spouse or nullification of the dissolution.

headings.title: Definition of relative of former spouse
headings.reviewNote: Defines relative of the settlor's former spouse as an individual related by blood, adoption, or affinity who is no longer related to the settlor after divorce.

headings.title: Tax exemptions for marital deduction trusts
headings.reviewNote: Exempts trusts qualifying for the federal gift tax marital deduction under IRC Section 2523 and precludes application that would cause adverse federal gift or estate tax consequences.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 456.1-112 governing revocation of spousal trust provisions upon divorce, exceptions, revival upon remarriage, definitions, and federal tax protections.

headings.title: Construction of terms of familial relationship
headings.reviewNote: Establishes rules for construing descendants, issue, and children in trust instruments regarding children born of marriage, children born out of wedlock, and adoption.

headings.title: Prospective application of established relationships
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that child rights following establishment of a parent-child relationship apply prospectively from the date of establishment without retroactive effect.

headings.title: Primacy of trust terms over familial definitions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that express terms of a trust prevail over the statutory familial relationship construction rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.1-114 on construing terms of familial relationships, non-retroactivity of established child status, and supremacy of express trust terms.

headings.title: Definition of breach of trust
headings.reviewNote: Defines a breach of trust as any violation by a trustee of a duty owed to a beneficiary.

headings.title: Judicial remedies to redress breach of trust
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates ten judicial remedies to prevent or redress a breach of trust, including compelling performance, enjoining breaches, requiring restitution or accounting, appointing special fiduciaries, or removal.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.10-1001 defining a breach of trust and specifying judicial remedies available to compel performance or redress violations.

headings.title: Measure of damages for breach of trust
headings.reviewNote: Holds a breaching trustee liable for the greater of the amount required to restore trust property and distributions or the profit the trustee made by reason of the breach.

headings.title: Contribution among liable cotrustees and limitations
headings.reviewNote: Provides for contribution among jointly liable trustees, subject to exceptions for trustees substantially more at fault, acting in bad faith, or benefiting from the breach.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.10-1002 governing the measure of damages for breach of trust and rights and limitations on contribution among cotrustees.

headings.title: Accountability for profits absent breach of trust
headings.reviewNote: Requires a trustee to account to affected beneficiaries for any profit made arising from administration of the trust even in the absence of a breach.

headings.title: Non-liability for losses absent breach of trust
headings.reviewNote: Insulates a trustee from liability for loss or depreciation in value of trust property or failure to make a profit absent a breach of trust.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.10-1003 governing trustee accountability for profits and non-liability for losses in the absence of a breach of trust.

headings.title: One-year limitation following adequate report and notice
headings.reviewNote: Bars beneficiary proceeding against trustee more than one year after report adequately disclosing potential claim and notice of limitation period.

headings.title: Adequacy of disclosure in trustee report
headings.reviewNote: Defines adequate disclosure as providing sufficient information so that the beneficiary or representative knows or should have inquired into the existence of the potential claim.

headings.title: Five-year limitation period upon specified termination events
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a five-year limitation period from trustee removal, resignation, death, termination of beneficiary's interest, or trust termination if the one-year bar does not apply.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.10-1005 establishing the 1-year limitation period following report disclosure, disclosure adequacy standards, and default 5-year limitations.

headings.title: Unenforceability of exculpatory terms for bad faith
headings.reviewNote: Renders unenforceable exculpatory terms relieving a trustee of liability for breaches committed in bad faith, with reckless indifference, or inserted through abuse of confidential relationship.

headings.title: Invalidity of trustee-drafted exculpatory terms
headings.reviewNote: Invalidates trustee-drafted exculpatory terms unless the settlor had independent counsel or the trustee proves fairness and adequate communication.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.10-1008 governing enforceability limits on trust exculpatory clauses and rules for trustee-drafted terms.

headings.title: Non-liability on contracts entered in fiduciary capacity
headings.reviewNote: Protects a trustee from personal liability on contracts entered into in a fiduciary capacity if the fiduciary capacity was disclosed in the contract.

headings.title: Personal liability for torts requiring personal fault
headings.reviewNote: Limits trustee personal liability for torts or obligations arising from ownership or control of trust property to situations where the trustee is personally at fault.

headings.title: Assertion of claims against trustee in fiduciary capacity
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes asserting claims based on contract or tort against the trustee in a fiduciary capacity regardless of the trustee's personal liability.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.10-1010 on trustee personal liability limits for disclosed contracts, personal fault requirement for torts, and proceedings against trustees in fiduciary capacity.

headings.title: Non-liability on partnership contracts when capacity disclosed
headings.reviewNote: Shields a trustee holding a general partner interest from personal liability on partnership contracts entered after acquisition (unless imposed by contract or excluded by subsection 3) if fiduciary capacity was disclosed in the contract or a prior secretary of state filing.

headings.title: Personal fault required for partnership tort liability
headings.reviewNote: Shields a trustee holding a general partner interest from personal liability for partnership torts or ownership/control obligations unless the trustee is personally at fault (subject to subsection 3).

headings.title: Exception for personal or family partnership interests
headings.reviewNote: Precludes section immunity if a partnership interest is held by the trustee in another capacity or by the trustee's spouse, descendants, siblings, parents, or any of their spouses.

headings.title: Settlor liability for revocable trust partnership interest
headings.reviewNote: Holds the settlor of a revocable trust whose trustee holds a general partner interest personally liable for partnership contracts and obligations as if the settlor were a general partner.

entries.reviewSummary: Personal liability protections for trustees holding general partnership interests on contracts and torts, family/individual interest exceptions, and settlor liability for revocable trusts.

headings.title: Protection of third parties dealing in good faith
headings.reviewNote: Protects a person other than a beneficiary who in good faith assists a trustee or deals for value with a trustee without knowledge of improper power exercise as if properly exercised.

headings.title: No duty to inquire into trustee powers
headings.reviewNote: Relieves a person other than a beneficiary dealing in good faith with a trustee from any duty to inquire into the extent of the trustee's powers or propriety of their exercise.

headings.title: No duty to oversee proper asset application
headings.reviewNote: Relieves a person who in good faith delivers assets to a trustee from ensuring their proper application.

headings.title: Protection for good-faith dealings with former trustee
headings.reviewNote: Protects a person other than a beneficiary who in good faith assists or deals for value with a former trustee without knowledge that the trusteeship has terminated.

headings.title: Supremacy of commercial and securities transfer laws
headings.reviewNote: Provides that comparable protective provisions of other laws relating to commercial transactions or fiduciary transfer of securities prevail over this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Good-faith protection for non-beneficiaries dealing with trustees or former trustees, no duty to inquire or oversee asset application, and supremacy of commercial and securities transfer laws.

headings.title: Certification of trust in lieu of instrument
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes trustee to provide a certification of trust containing eight enumerated pieces of administrative information instead of furnishing the full trust instrument.

headings.title: Execution by all trustees and acknowledgment
headings.reviewNote: Requires certification of trust to be signed by all trustees and allows third parties to require acknowledgment or guarantee.

headings.title: Required statement regarding nonrevocation and accuracy
headings.reviewNote: Requires certification to state that the trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in a manner that would cause representations to be incorrect.

headings.title: Omission of dispositive terms permitted
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a certification of trust need not contain the dispositive terms of the trust.

headings.title: Recipient right to request trust excerpts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a recipient of a certification of trust to require excerpts designating the trustee and conferring relevant transaction powers.

headings.title: Immunity for reliance on certification of trust
headings.reviewNote: Protects a person acting in reliance on a certification of trust without knowledge of incorrect representations from liability.

headings.title: Enforceability of transactions against trust property
headings.reviewNote: Permits a person entering into a transaction in good faith reliance on a certification to enforce the transaction against trust property.

headings.title: Liability for bad-faith demand for instrument
headings.reviewNote: Imposes damages liability on a person who demands the trust instrument in bad faith in addition to the certification or excerpts.

headings.title: Preservation of discovery rights in judicial proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not limit rights to obtain copies of the trust instrument in a judicial proceeding.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsections for 456.10-1013 governing contents, execution, third-party reliance protections, and bad-faith demand penalties for certifications of trust.

headings.title: Presumption of unlimited authority for power of appointment
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a statutory presumption that a power of appointment is presently exercisable, exclusionary, and general, subject to classification rules.

headings.title: Nongeneral classification for testamentary power with limited class
headings.reviewNote: Classifies a power of appointment as nongeneral if exercisable only at death and permissible appointees are a limited class excluding powerholder, estate, and creditors.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.1000 setting statutory presumptions of unlimited authority for powers of appointment and criteria for nongeneral classification.

headings.title: Definition of adverse party
headings.reviewNote: Defines adverse party as a person with a substantial beneficial interest that would be adversely affected by exercise or nonexercise in favor of powerholder or creditors.

headings.title: Nongeneral classification with adverse party consent requirement
headings.reviewNote: Classifies a power of appointment as nongeneral if it may be exercised only with the consent or joinder of an adverse party.

headings.title: Exclusionary classification when permissible appointees unlimited
headings.reviewNote: Classifies a power of appointment as exclusionary if its permissible appointees are not defined and limited.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.1005 defining adverse party and providing classification rules for powers requiring adverse party joinder and exclusionary powers.

headings.title: Definitions of residuary clause and will
headings.reviewNote: Defines residuary clause excluding blanket or specific exercise clauses, and defines will including codicils and revising testamentary instruments.

headings.title: Circumstances manifesting intent through residuary clause
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a residuary clause manifests intent to exercise a power of appointment only if the power is general, has no effective gift in default, and was not released.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.1020 defining relevant testamentary terms and limiting when a residuary clause manifests intent to exercise a power of appointment.

headings.title: Application of blanket-exercise clause to after-acquired power
headings.reviewNote: Establishes general rule that a blanket-exercise clause extends to a power of appointment acquired by the powerholder after executing the instrument.

headings.title: Exception when powerholder is also donor
headings.reviewNote: Precludes extension of a blanket-exercise clause to an after-acquired power if the powerholder is also the donor, unless the gift-in-default clause is missing or ineffective.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.1025 governing the extension of blanket-exercise clauses to after-acquired powers of appointment and donor-powerholder exceptions.

headings.title: Scope of appointment under general power
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a powerholder of a general power exercisable in favor of self or estate to make any appointment, including in trust or creating new powers, as with owned property.

headings.title: Limitation on appointment under creditor general power
headings.reviewNote: Restricts appointment under a general power exercisable only in favor of creditors to those creditors.

headings.title: Permissible appointments under nongeneral power
headings.reviewNote: Specifies permissible forms of appointment under a nongeneral power, including appointments in trust, creating powers in permissible appointees, or creating nongeneral powers in others.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.1035 delineating permissible appointments under general powers, creditor-only general powers, and nongeneral powers.

headings.title: Ineffectiveness of appointment to deceased appointee
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an appointment to a deceased appointee is ineffective.

headings.title: Exercise in favor of deceased appointee descendant
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes powerholder of a nongeneral power to exercise the power in favor of, or create new powers in, descendants of a deceased permissible appointee.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.1040 rendering appointments to deceased appointees ineffective and authorizing appointments to descendants of deceased permissible appointees.

headings.title: Ineffectiveness of exercise for impermissible appointee
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an exercise of a power of appointment in favor of an impermissible appointee is ineffective, subject to section 456.1040.

headings.title: Ineffectiveness of appointment constituting fraud on power
headings.reviewNote: Renders ineffective an appointment in favor of a permissible appointee to the extent that it constitutes a fraud on the power.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.1045 governing the ineffectiveness of appointments to impermissible appointees and appointments constituting a fraud on the power.

headings.title: Sharing in unappointed property after partial appointment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a taker in default of appointment who receives a valid partial appointment to share fully in unappointed property.

headings.title: Treatment of appointment identical to default gift
headings.reviewNote: Treats an appointment to a taker in default as ineffective if the appointee would have taken the same property in the same form and amount under a gift-in-default clause.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.1070 on rights of takers in default after partial appointments and the effect of appointments duplicating gifts in default.

headings.title: Powerholder authority to release power of appointment
headings.reviewNote: Permits a powerholder to release a power of appointment in whole or in part except to the extent prevented by the terms of the creating instrument.

headings.title: Methods of releasing power of appointment
headings.reviewNote: Permits release by substantial compliance with the instrument's method or, if none is exclusively specified, by a clear-and-convincing instrument delivered to the donor, personal representative, guardian/conservator, or legal title holder, with permissive probate division filing.

headings.title: Revocation or amendment of instrument of release
headings.reviewNote: Restricts revocation or amendment of a release to situations where the instrument is revocable or the powerholder reserved the right to revoke or amend.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.1085 governing authority to release powers of appointment, delivery and filing procedures, and limits on revocation of releases.

headings.title: Contract regarding presently exercisable power of appointment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a powerholder of a presently exercisable power to contract not to exercise the power, or to exercise it if no benefit is conferred on an impermissible appointee.

headings.title: Contract regarding power not presently exercisable
headings.reviewNote: Permits contracting to exercise or not exercise a power not presently exercisable only if the powerholder is also the donor and reserved the power in a revocable trust.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.1090 specifying rules and enforceability limits for contracts concerning presently exercisable and not presently exercisable powers of appointment.

headings.title: Application of Uniform Trust Code to existing trusts
headings.reviewNote: Applies the UTC on January 1, 2005, to existing and future trusts, judicial proceedings, and construction rules, preserves prior acts, and excludes section 456.590 (source footnote notes repealed by H.B. 1765, 2016) from post-2004 instruments.

headings.title: Preservation of running limitation periods under prior law
headings.reviewNote: Preserves the continued application of prior statutes regarding rights acquired, extinguished, or barred upon expiration of prescribed periods commencing before January 1, 2005.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.11-1106 detailing transitional rules and effective-date application of the Missouri Uniform Trust Code to existing trusts and legal proceedings.

headings.title: Definition of power created by powerholder
headings.reviewNote: Defines power of appointment created by the powerholder to include powers created in transfers by others where the powerholder contributed value.

headings.title: Creditor claims against appointive property under chapter 428
headings.reviewNote: Subjects appointive property under a general power created by the powerholder to claims of creditors of the powerholder or estate under chapter 428 fraudulent transfer law.

headings.title: Exemptions for irrevocably appointed property and unexercisable powers
headings.reviewNote: Shields appointive property from creditor claims to the extent irrevocably appointed to another or where the general power is not presently exercisable.

headings.title: Creditor access to presently exercisable general power
headings.reviewNote: Subjects appointive property under a presently exercisable general power created by the powerholder to creditor claims as if owned property, notwithstanding spendthrift terms.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 456.1100 governing creditor access to appointive property under general powers created by the powerholder, chapter 428 limits, and spendthrift overrides.

headings.title: Creditor access when powerholder property insufficient
headings.reviewNote: Subjects appointive property under an exercisable general power created by another (source footnote notes word 'a' appears in original rolls) to creditor claims to the extent the powerholder's property is insufficient.

headings.title: Exemption for testamentary or unexercisable general powers
headings.reviewNote: Exempts appointive property under a testamentary or not presently exercisable general power created by another from creditor claims against the powerholder or estate.

headings.title: Treatment of powers with ascertainable standards
headings.reviewNote: Treats a power created by another that is subject to an ascertainable standard for health, education, support, or maintenance as a nongeneral power for creditor claims.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.1105 governing creditor claims against general powers created by others, testamentary power exemptions, and ascertainable standard treatment.

headings.title: Treatment of withdrawal power during exercise period
headings.reviewNote: Treats a power of withdrawal during the exercise period as a presently exercisable general power of appointment to the extent of property subject to the power.

headings.title: Treatment upon lapse or release of withdrawal power
headings.reviewNote: Treats lapsed, released, or waived withdrawal powers as presently exercisable general powers only to the extent the value exceeds statutory IRC 2041(b)(2), 2514(e), or 2503(b) thresholds.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.1110 equating withdrawal powers to presently exercisable general powers during life and limiting post-lapse exposure to amounts above tax exclusions.

headings.title: Exemption of nongeneral power from creditor claims
headings.reviewNote: Exempts appointive property subject to a nongeneral power of appointment from claims of creditors of the powerholder or estate, subject to statutory exceptions.

headings.title: Exception for fraudulent transfer by powerholder
headings.reviewNote: Subjects nongeneral appointive property to creditor claims to the extent the powerholder owned the property and transferred it in violation of chapter 428 fraudulent transfer law.

headings.title: Treatment where initial default gift to powerholder
headings.reviewNote: Treats a nongeneral power as a general power for creditor claims if the initial gift in default of appointment is to the powerholder or the powerholder's estate.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.1115 providing creditor exemptions for nongeneral powers of appointment, with fraudulent transfer and self-default exceptions.

headings.title: Application of powers act to existing relationships
headings.reviewNote: Applies sections 456.970 to 456.1135 to powers of appointment created before, on, or after August 28, 2016, and pending proceedings unless causing substantial prejudice.

headings.title: Preservation of running limitation periods under prior law
headings.reviewNote: Preserves the continued operation of prior law for rights acquired, extinguished, or barred upon expiration of prescribed periods starting before August 28, 2016.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.1135 governing the 2016 effective-date application of the Uniform Powers of Appointment Act to existing powers and legal proceedings.

headings.title: Court intervention limited to invoked jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the court may intervene in trust administration only to the extent its jurisdiction is invoked by an interested person or as provided by law.

headings.title: Exemption from continuing judicial supervision
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that a trust is not subject to continuing judicial supervision unless ordered by the court.

headings.title: Scope of administration proceedings and instructions
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that judicial proceedings may relate to any matter of trust administration, including requests for instructions and actions to declare rights.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.2-201 establishing the limited role of courts in trust administration without continuing judicial supervision.

headings.title: Trustee submission to personal jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Provides that by accepting trusteeship of a Missouri-administered trust or moving administration to Missouri, the trustee submits personally to court jurisdiction.

headings.title: Beneficiary submission and recipient personal jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Subjects beneficiaries to court jurisdiction regarding trust administration, and subjects distribution recipients personally to jurisdiction.

headings.title: Matters subject to judicial administration proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates 21 non-exclusive administration matters subject to judicial proceedings, including instructions, validity, accounting, removal, and termination.

headings.title: Preservation of other methods of obtaining jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not preclude other statutory or constitutional methods of obtaining jurisdiction over trustees, beneficiaries, or recipients.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 456.2-202 establishing personal jurisdiction rules over trustees, beneficiaries, and distributees, and listing 21 administration proceedings.

headings.title: Venue for registered and unregistered trusts
headings.reviewNote: Places venue in the probate division where the trust is registered, where an unregistered trust could properly be registered, or under civil procedure rules if it cannot properly be registered in Missouri.

headings.title: Exclusive right of court where first commenced
headings.reviewNote: Grants the court in which a judicial proceeding is first commenced the exclusive right to proceed when venue could be maintained in more than one place in Missouri.

headings.title: Priority and transfer between multiple proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Directs that when proceedings are commenced in multiple courts, the first court hears the matter while others hold cases in abeyance, transferring venue if appropriate.

headings.title: Court transfer in interest of justice
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to transfer a proceeding or file to another court in this state in the interest of justice.

entries.reviewSummary: Venue for registered and unregistered trust proceedings, exclusive priority of first-commenced proceedings, abeyance and venue transfer among multiple courts, and interest-of-justice transfers.

headings.title: Enforceability of mandatory mediation or arbitration provisions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a provision in a trust instrument requiring mediation or arbitration of disputes among beneficiaries, fiduciaries, or powerholders is enforceable.

headings.title: Consent required for arbitration of trust validity
headings.reviewNote: Precludes enforcement of mediation or arbitration clauses for disputes concerning the validity of a trust unless all interested persons consent.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.2-205 enforcing arbitration and mediation clauses for internal trust disputes while requiring unanimous consent for trust validity contests.

headings.title: Effect of notice given to representative
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that notice given to a person authorized to represent and bind another under the representation rules has the same effect as direct notice.

headings.title: Binding effect of representative consent and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Makes representative consent binding unless objected to before taking effect, except it binds regardless of objection for testamentary powerholders, conservators/guardians (source footnote notes 'subdivisions' in original rolls), and parents of minor/unborn children.

headings.title: Representation of incapacitated settlor
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes an eligible representative to receive notice and give binding consent on behalf of a settlor who lacks capacity, subject to statutory limits.

headings.title: Settlor prohibited from representing beneficiary in modification
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a settlor from representing and binding a beneficiary with respect to trust modification or termination under section 456.4-411A.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 456.3-301 governing basic effects of virtual representation, notice, binding consent, representation of incapacitated settlors, and conflict restrictions.

headings.title: Representation by holder of substantially identical interest
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes representation of a minor, incapacitated, unborn, or unascertainable person by another holding a substantially identical interest without conflict of interest.

headings.title: Representation of non-qualified beneficiary by qualified beneficiary
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a qualified beneficiary with a substantially identical interest and no conflict to represent a non-qualified beneficiary in judicial modification or nonjudicial settlements.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.3-304 governing virtual representation by individuals having substantially identical interests in litigation and nonjudicial settlements.

headings.title: Court appointment of representative for unrepresented interests
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to appoint a representative to receive notice, give consent, and act on behalf of a minor, incapacitated, unborn, or unknown person.

headings.title: Representative authority in pending and non-pending matters
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes an appointed representative to act with respect to any matter under the Missouri Uniform Trust Code whether or not judicial proceedings are pending.

headings.title: Consideration of general family benefits by representative
headings.reviewNote: Permits an appointed representative in making decisions to consider general benefits accruing to living members of the individual's family.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.3-305 authorizing court appointment of representatives for unrepresented interests, delineating powers, and permitting consideration of family benefits.

headings.title: Mandatory requirements for creating valid trust
headings.reviewNote: Sets forth the five essential requirements for trust creation: settlor capacity, intention, definite or permitted purpose beneficiary, trustee duties, and separation of sole trustee and beneficiary.

headings.title: Standard for definite beneficiary
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a beneficiary is definite if ascertainable now or in the future subject to applicable rules against perpetuities.

headings.title: Trustee power to select from indefinite class
headings.reviewNote: Validates a power in a trustee to select a beneficiary from an indefinite class and provides for failure if not exercised within a reasonable time.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.4-402 specifying core requirements for trust creation, definite beneficiary criteria, and powers to select from indefinite classes.

headings.title: Permissible purposes of charitable trust
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates recognized charitable purposes including relief of poverty, education, religion, health promotion, governmental purposes, and community benefit.

headings.title: Court selection of charitable purpose or beneficiary
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to select charitable purposes or beneficiaries consistent with the settlor's intent if the trust terms do not specify them.

headings.title: Standing of settlor and others to enforce
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the settlor, among others, to maintain a proceeding to enforce a charitable trust.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.4-405 defining charitable trust purposes, court selection authority for unspecified beneficiaries, and enforcement standing.

headings.title: Clear and convincing standard for oral trust
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an oral trust does not require a written instrument but its creation and terms must be established by clear and convincing evidence.

headings.title: Writing requirement for trusts of land
headings.reviewNote: Requires trusts of lands, tenements, or hereditaments to be manifested and proved by a signed writing or will to avoid invalidity under the statute of frauds.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.4-407 establishing the clear and convincing evidence standard for oral personal property trusts and written proof requirements for trusts of land.

headings.title: Creation and termination of animal trust
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes creation of a trust for the care of animals alive during the settlor's lifetime, terminating upon the death of the animal or the last surviving animal.

headings.title: Enforcement of animal care trust
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an animal trust may be enforced by a person appointed in the terms of the trust or appointed by the court upon application of an interested person.

headings.title: Distribution of property exceeding intended use
headings.reviewNote: Directs that trust property exceeding the amount required for the intended animal care must be distributed to the settlor or successors unless the trust provides otherwise.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.4-408 governing validity, termination, enforcement standing, and distribution of excess property for animal care trusts.

headings.title: Circumstances resulting in trust termination
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a trust terminates to the extent revoked or expired, no purpose remains to be achieved, or purposes have become unlawful, contrary to public policy, or impossible.

headings.title: Standing to petition for modification or termination
headings.reviewNote: Permits a trustee or beneficiary to commence modification, termination, combination, or division proceedings under sections 456.4-411A to 456.4-417, permits a settlor under section 456.4-411A, and permits a charitable trust settlor to seek cy pres modification under section 456.4-413.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.4-410 establishing termination grounds for expired or impossible purposes and standing to petition for judicial modification or termination.

headings.title: Modification or termination by settlor and beneficiary consent
headings.reviewNote: Permits modifying or terminating a noncharitable irrevocable trust (except court-established special trusts) without court approval upon consent of the settlor (or authorized agent/court-approved conservator) and all beneficiaries, even if inconsistent with a material purpose.

headings.title: Distribution of property as agreed by beneficiaries
headings.reviewNote: Requires the trustee, upon termination under subsection 1, to distribute the trust property as agreed by the beneficiaries.

headings.title: Court approval when not all beneficiaries consent
headings.reviewNote: Permits court approval of a proposed subsection 1 modification or termination without all beneficiaries' consent if it would be valid with full consent and nonconsenting beneficiaries' interests will be adequately protected.

entries.reviewSummary: Nonjudicial modification or termination of noncharitable irrevocable trusts by consent of settlor and all beneficiaries, property distribution on termination, and court approval with partial beneficiary consent.

headings.title: Beneficiary consent to modify or terminate trust
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court modification or termination of a noncharitable irrevocable trust upon consent of all competent adult beneficiaries upon finding nonconsenting interests adequately protected.

headings.title: Distribution of property upon court-ordered termination
headings.reviewNote: Requires the trustee to distribute trust property as directed by the court upon termination under subsection 1.

headings.title: Court approval when beneficiary consent is incomplete
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court approval of modification or termination without complete beneficiary consent if nonconsenting interests are protected and continuance is not necessary for a material purpose.

headings.title: Replacement of prior law and universal applicability
headings.reviewNote: Replaces repealed section 456.590 and applies to all trusts created under instruments that become irrevocable prior to, on, or after January 1, 2005.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 456.4-411B governing judicial modification and termination of noncharitable irrevocable trusts upon beneficiary consent, material purpose findings, and universal applicability.

headings.title: Modification of dispositive terms for unanticipated circumstances
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to modify dispositive terms or terminate a trust if unanticipated circumstances arise and modification will further trust purposes in accordance with settlor's probable intent.

headings.title: Modification of administrative terms to further purposes
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to modify management or administrative terms of a trust if modification will further the purposes of the trust.

headings.title: Distribution of property consistent with trust purposes
headings.reviewNote: Requires the trustee to distribute trust property in a manner consistent with the purposes of the trust upon termination under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.4-412 governing court modification of dispositive or administrative terms and termination due to unanticipated circumstances.

headings.title: Application of cy pres to charitable trusts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to apply cy pres to modify or terminate a charitable trust when a particular purpose becomes unlawful, impracticable, impossible, or wasteful, directing property consistent with settlor's charitable purposes.

headings.title: Distribution to noncharitable beneficiary prevailing over cy pres
headings.reviewNote: Provides that trust terms directing reversion to settlor or distribution to noncharitable beneficiaries prevail over cy pres only if settlor is living or fewer than 21 years have elapsed.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.4-413 providing cy pres modification and termination for charitable trusts and conditions where noncharitable gift-overs prevail.

headings.title: Trustee termination of trust under statutory threshold
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the trustee to terminate a trust under $250,000 upon notice to qualified beneficiaries if the property is insufficient to justify administration costs.

headings.title: Court modification, termination, or trustee removal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to modify or terminate a trust or replace the trustee if trust property value is insufficient to justify administration costs.

headings.title: Distribution of property upon uneconomic termination
headings.reviewNote: Requires the trustee to distribute trust property in a manner consistent with trust purposes upon termination under this section.

headings.title: Inapplicability to conservation easements
headings.reviewNote: Exempts conservation or preservation easements from the uneconomic trust modification and termination provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsections for 456.4-414 governing trustee termination of trusts under $250,000, court modification powers, distribution rules, and conservation easement exemptions.

headings.title: Discretionary distributions to qualified remainder beneficiary
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes trustee discretion to distribute trust income or principal to a qualified remainder beneficiary, defined as a descendant of a permissible distributee.

headings.title: Conditions for application to pre-1985 irrevocable trust
headings.reviewNote: Sets forth six prerequisite conditions for section applicability to pre-September 25, 1985 irrevocable trusts, including 10-year distribution hiatus and tax neutrality.

headings.title: Events terminating application of distribution authority
headings.reviewNote: Specifies events terminating section applicability, including death of all permissible distributees, trust termination, or impairment of obligations.

headings.title: Effect of spendthrift clause on distribution authority
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that a spendthrift provision in the trust terms is not presumed inconsistent with applying this section to the trust.

headings.title: Advance notice requirement to qualified beneficiaries
headings.reviewNote: Requires trustee to give at least sixty days' notice to qualified beneficiaries prior to distributing income or principal to a qualified remainder beneficiary.

headings.title: Trustee immunity for good-faith actions
headings.reviewNote: Insulates a trustee acting in good faith from liability to any beneficiary for acting or failing to act under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsections for 456.4-418 governing discretionary distributions to qualified remainder beneficiaries of pre-1985 trusts, notice, and trustee immunity.

headings.title: Trustee discretionary decanting power to second trust
headings.reviewNote: Permits a non-settlor trustee with discretionary distribution power, unless expressly prohibited, to distribute property to one or more second trusts or modify the first trust into one or more second trusts.

headings.title: Second-trust beneficiary and power of appointment rules
headings.reviewNote: Sets five rules for second trusts: retaining at least one permissible distributee, living non-grantor vs. deceased/grantor trust distributee rules, prohibiting non-first-trust beneficiaries, and retaining, modifying, omitting, or creating powers of appointment.

headings.title: Special-needs decanting for beneficiaries with disabilities
headings.reviewNote: Defines disability and special-needs trust terms and permits a special-needs fiduciary to decant into a special-needs trust (including Medicaid pooled or payback trusts under 42 U.S.C. Section 1396p(d)(4)) while preserving other beneficiaries' substantially similar interests.

headings.title: Ascertainable standard, tax, withdrawal, and spendthrift limits
headings.reviewNote: Limits decanting by trustee-beneficiaries under ascertainable standards, preserves marital, charitable, gift exclusion, S-corporation, and GST tax qualifications, protects presently exercisable withdrawal powers, and states spendthrift or no-amendment clauses do not bar decanting.

headings.title: Sixty-day notice to permissible distributees and waiver
headings.reviewNote: Requires notifying permissible distributees of the first and second trusts at least sixty days before a decanting distribution, and permits beneficiaries to waive notice or withdraw a prior waiver for future distributions.

headings.title: Continued application of trustee fiduciary duties
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a trustee exercising decanting authority remains subject to all fiduciary duties imposed under the trust instrument and Missouri law.

headings.title: No duty to exercise or consider decanting
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section imposes no duty on a trustee to exercise or to consider exercising decanting authority in favor of another trust.

headings.title: Second-trust duration and perpetuity rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits a different duration for a second trust while subjecting attributable property to first-trust perpetuity, accumulation, and alienation rules, without precluding creation of a general power of appointment.

headings.title: Savings rules for partially noncompliant second trusts
headings.reviewNote: Preserves effectiveness of a partially noncompliant decanting by voiding unpermitted second-trust provisions and deeming omitted required provisions included to the extent necessary to comply.

headings.title: Codification of common law and Missouri-law applicability
headings.reviewNote: States legislative intent to codify and limit Missouri common law and applies the section to any trust governed by Missouri law, including trusts whose principal place of administration is transferred to Missouri.

entries.reviewSummary: Missouri trust decanting authority, second-trust beneficiary and power-of-appointment rules, special-needs decanting, tax and withdrawal-right limitations, 60-day notice, fiduciary duties, duration, savings clause, and Missouri-law scope.

headings.title: Interlocutory petition on no-contest clause applicability
headings.reviewNote: Permits an interested person under an irrevocable trust containing a no-contest clause to petition for an interlocutory determination whether a particular claim would trigger the clause or an enforceable forfeiture.

headings.title: Verified petition, priority ruling, and evidentiary limits
headings.reviewNote: Requires verification under oath, allows separate or joined filing with priority ruling before other claims, and limits court review to the clause, trust instrument, and pleadings unless needed to resolve ambiguity.

headings.title: Appealability, stay pending appeal, and later claims
headings.reviewNote: Subjects orders to final or interlocutory appeal, permits staying pending proceedings during interlocutory appeal, and provides that a final ruling does not preclude later filing of other trust claims.

headings.title: Binding enforcement effect and reversal protection
headings.reviewNote: Makes the no-contest clause enforceable to the extent of the court's ruling if the party proceeds, and protects interested persons from prejudice for relying on an order later vacated, reversed, or modified.

headings.title: Order limited to recited trust terms and facts
headings.reviewNote: Limits the order's effect strictly to the trust terms and factual basis recited in the petition, denying protection for later materially different claims.

headings.title: Definition of no-contest and in terrorem clauses
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'no-contest clause' (also 'in terrorem clause') as a trust term rescinding a donative transfer or fiduciary appointment or effecting forfeiture for beneficiary action, without determining general enforceability.

headings.title: Circumstances where no-contest clause is unenforceable
headings.reviewNote: Lists seven non-exclusive circumstances where a no-contest clause is unenforceable, including jurisdiction/venue objections, accounting/report claims, chapter 475/404 petitions, lawful disclosures, nonjudicial settlement approval, and subsection 1 petitions.

headings.title: Discretionary award of attorney fees and costs
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court to award costs, expenses, and attorneys' fees to any party under section 456.10-1004 in proceedings brought under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Interlocutory petitions to determine no-contest clause applicability, verified pleading and priority ruling rules, appealability, scope of binding effect, definition, unenforceable circumstances, and fee awards.

headings.title: Validity requirements for spendthrift provision
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a spendthrift provision is valid if it restrains either the voluntary or involuntary transfer, or both the voluntary and involuntary transfer, of a beneficiary's interest.

headings.title: Language sufficient to create spendthrift trust
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that terms stating the interest of a beneficiary is held subject to a spendthrift trust, or words of similar import, are sufficient to restrain transfers.

headings.title: Effect of spendthrift protection against creditors
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a beneficiary may not transfer a spendthrift interest and creditors or assignees cannot reach the interest before distribution.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.5-502 establishing validity requirements, drafting language, and protective effects against creditors for spendthrift provisions.

headings.title: Definitions of child and judgment
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'child' (any person with a child support order or judgment in Missouri or another state) and 'judgment' (a judgment executable in Missouri) for this section.

headings.title: Exceptions for support and trust-protection creditors
headings.reviewNote: Permits a beneficiary's child, spouse, or former spouse with a support/maintenance judgment, or a judgment creditor who provided services protecting the beneficiary's trust interest, to obtain an order attaching present or future trust income, with equitable relief if multiple permissible distributees exist.

headings.title: Exception for federal and state claims
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a spendthrift provision is unenforceable against a claim of the state of Missouri or the United States to the extent provided by other laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Definitions of child and judgment, spendthrift exceptions for support/maintenance judgments and trust-interest protection creditors, and unenforceability against state or federal statutory claims.

headings.title: Discretionary interest not property right
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a beneficiary has no property right or enforceable interest in a discretionary trust distribution, and creditors cannot compel distributions even with standards.

headings.title: Beneficiary right to challenge abuse of discretion
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not limit a beneficiary's right to maintain a judicial proceeding against a trustee for abuse of discretion or failure to comply with a distribution standard.

headings.title: Applicability regardless of spendthrift provision
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section applies whether or not a beneficiary's interest is subject to a spendthrift provision.

headings.title: Discretionary interest defined by non-mandatory status
headings.reviewNote: Defines an interest as subject to trustee discretion if it does not constitute a mandatory distribution as defined in subsection 1 of section 456.5-506.

headings.title: Creditor barred from trust asset and record information
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits creditors or claimants from obtaining any information on trust assets or records during the trust term if distributions to the beneficiary are solely within trustee discretion, regardless of spendthrift terms or remainder status.

entries.reviewSummary: Discretionary trust interests as non-property barred from creditor attachment, preserved beneficiary abuse-of-discretion claims, spendthrift irrelevance, non-mandatory definition, and bar on creditor record access.

headings.title: Creditor claims against revocable trust during life
headings.reviewNote: Subjects property of a revocable trust during the settlor's lifetime to claims of the settlor's creditors regardless of any spendthrift provision.

headings.title: Creditor claims against irrevocable trust without spendthrift
headings.reviewNote: Permits a settlor's creditor or assignee to reach the maximum amount distributable to or for the settlor from an irrevocable trust without a spendthrift provision, capped at the settlor's contribution if multiple settlors.

headings.title: Spendthrift protection for irrevocable trust and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Bars settlor's creditors from an irrevocable trust with a spendthrift provision except for chapter 428 fraudulent conveyances or where the settlor was sole beneficiary, retained amendment power, or retained a determinable specific portion.

headings.title: Settlor powers not defeating spendthrift protection
headings.reviewNote: Bars settlor's creditors from reaching the settlor's beneficial interest in a subsection 3 trust despite a nongeneral testamentary power of appointment or a power to veto trust distributions.

headings.title: Published post-death creditor notice and six-month bar
headings.reviewNote: Permits a trustee with power or duty to pay a deceased settlor's debts to publish a four-week newspaper notice in the specified domicile/asset/administration county, barring unpresented debts after six months and excusing section 461.300 accounting.

headings.title: Treatment of withdrawal powerholder as settlor
headings.reviewNote: Treats a powerholder of a withdrawal power as a settlor during the exercise period and limits post-lapse exposure to amounts above tax exclusions.

headings.title: Exclusion of second trusts from settlor status
headings.reviewNote: Excludes the settlor of specified irrevocable inter vivos trusts (marital deduction, spouse-exercised power, or general power exercise; source footnote notes 'section' in original rolls) from being treated as settlor of a second trust created by power of appointment.

headings.title: Exemption for section 456.014 spendthrift trusts
headings.reviewNote: Exempts spendthrift trusts described, defined, or established under section 456.014 from the provisions of this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Creditor claims against revocable trusts, irrevocable trusts with and without spendthrift provisions, protected settlor powers, post-death published creditor notice and 6-month bar, withdrawal powers, second-trust exclusions, and section 456.014 exemption.

headings.title: Definition of mandatory distribution
headings.reviewNote: Defines mandatory distribution as a required distribution of income or principal, excluding discretionary distributions even if coupled with standards.

headings.title: Creditor access to overdue mandatory distribution
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a creditor or assignee to reach a mandatory distribution if the trustee fails to make it within a reasonable time after the required date, regardless of spendthrift terms.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsections for 456.5-506 defining mandatory distributions and permitting creditors to reach overdue distributions notwithstanding spendthrift clauses.

headings.title: Appointive property exempt from creditor claims
headings.reviewNote: Exempts appointive property subject to a testamentary general power or a nongeneral power from creditor claims, subject to sections 456.970 to 456.1135.

headings.title: Preservation of remedies against beneficial interests
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not limit a creditor's ability to reach a beneficiary's separate beneficial interest under sections 456.5-501 to 456.5-507.

headings.title: Incorporation of definitions from powers act
headings.reviewNote: Incorporates statutory definitions of appointive property, general power, nongeneral power, and creditor claim from section 456.975.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsections for 456.5-508 shielding appointive property under testamentary general and nongeneral powers from creditor claims, while preserving remedies against beneficial interests.

headings.title: Settlor power to revoke or amend trust
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the settlor to revoke or amend a trust unless the terms expressly provide that it is irrevocable, applying to trusts executed on or after January 1, 2005.

headings.title: Revocation and amendment by multiple settlors
headings.reviewNote: Specifies revocation and amendment rules for trusts with multiple settlors, covering community property and separate contributions.

headings.title: Permissible methods of revocation or amendment
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a settlor may revoke or amend by substantially complying with trust methods or by any other method manifesting clear and convincing evidence, including later wills.

headings.title: Delivery of trust property upon revocation
headings.reviewNote: Directs the trustee to deliver trust property as the settlor directs upon revocation of a revocable trust.

headings.title: Exercise of revocation powers by agent
headings.reviewNote: Restricts exercise of settlor revocation, amendment, or distribution powers by an agent under a power of attorney to express authorization in the trust or power.

headings.title: Exercise of settlor powers by conservator
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a settlor's conservator or conservator ad litem to exercise revocation or amendment powers only with approval of the supervising court.

headings.title: Trustee non-liability without knowledge of modification
headings.reviewNote: Protects a trustee lacking knowledge of trust revocation or amendment from liability for distributions and actions taken in good faith.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsections for 456.6-602 detailing settlor revocation and amendment powers, multiple settlors, methods, agents, conservators, and trustee protections.

headings.title: Trustee duties owed exclusively to competent settlor
headings.reviewNote: Provides that while a trust is revocable and the settlor has capacity, beneficiary rights are subject to settlor control and trustee duties are owed exclusively to the settlor.

headings.title: Presumption of capacity until adjudication or affidavit
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a presumption that the settlor has capacity until adjudicated incapacitated or disabled or until the trustee receives a physician's affidavit of incapacity.

headings.title: Duties owed to all competent co-settlors
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that if a revocable trust has more than one settlor, the trustee's duties are owed to all settlors having capacity to revoke.

headings.title: Rights of holder of withdrawal power
headings.reviewNote: Accords the holder of a power of withdrawal the rights of a settlor under this section to the extent of property subject to the power.

headings.title: Definition of affidavit of incapacity
headings.reviewNote: Defines affidavit of incapacity as a written certificate furnished by at least one licensed medical doctor stating the settlor lacks capacity to revoke.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsections for 456.6-603 governing trustee duties owed to settlors, capacity presumptions, multi-settlor rules, withdrawal rights, and medical affidavit definitions.

headings.title: Limitation periods for contesting revocable trust validity
